title: A certification reaches CC's bus address
owner: cairn (cairn/tools/base is the base tool's address; CC builds)
intention: Each certification a gate issues (a ticket's crossing, journaled by emit) reaches CC's bus address as one 'personal' message, so CC, today's builder, prover and every other summons handler, hears the event without standing at the gate.
why: Akien 2026-10-27, verbatim on open-a89d15043c7c: 'that certification being completed is an event. that event triggers probes for any device in the system that can handle that event... over the bus. no orchestrator'; on open-c345acf7f373: 'right now you are the builder and the prover and the so on... we can build out the pieces that would send you email for each of these event changes'; on open-a44f6aadde21: 'a message to your bus address', because mail is an open prompt-injection hole.
traces_to: Akien's answers on open-a89d15043c7c, open-c345acf7f373, open-a44f6aadde21; the bus intention (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/intention+why.json: the only device-to-device path); Law 1; ticket 1e2640bad4dd (PROVED: the receiving half, bus -> CC mailbox -> poke); ticket 48519f4789b1 decision 14 (the removed post this answers).
how: One never-raising function in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, called in emit right after projector.append_entry writes the crossing's journal. It lazily imports cairn.tools.bus_client.remote and posts through RemoteBus (the one bus process, never a private ring, never ensure_bus/connect_bus) one envelope: sender 'cairn', to 'cc', channel 'personal', verb 'certified', body {ticket, component, from, to, direction, fingerprint} plus the testing mark when CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID is set. Any failure is caught and reported on stderr; the crossing already stands. CC's shim (built) delivers and pokes. Decisions D1-D5.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a live crossing of a real ticket puts exactly one 'personal' envelope to 'cc' with verb 'certified' on the bus naming that ticket, component and summons, and ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail_ledger.jsonl shows it delivered (plus 'poked' if CC was idle); (2) with the bus unreachable, emit still journals, returns the new workflow string and raises nothing; (3) under CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID the body carries testing_mark.mark(<id>). (2)-(3) are proofs in cairn/tools/base/proofs/; (1) is measured live at PROVEME. WRONG INTENT if the mail-ledger rate shows notices CC never acts on, or if a second handler makes the address 'cc' a consumer registry, in which case the event moves to subscription.
watchme: none, because the falsifier's noise question is read directly from CC's mail ledger at /home/akien/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail_ledger.jsonl, which the cc device's mail probe already counts (ticket 1e2640bad4dd).

decisions.text: D2: PLACE. The post runs in emit after projector.append_entry and before _stamp_sail. The D14 comment at that spot is rewritten to cite this ticket and say how both of D14's whys are answered: the one bus process replaces the unflushed private ring, and the post comes after the journal, off the verdict path. Import lazily inside the function; never call ensure_bus or connect_bus (they spawn a bus).

D3: BODY. {ticket, component (history_path's parent relative to the cairn root), from, to, direction ('forward'|'back'), fingerprint (record['fingerprint'])}. Never ticket content: CC reads the ticket through its own door. why = 'certified: <ticket> <from> -> <to>'. Every ticket-carrying crossing emit journals is sent, forward and back; noise is measured from the mail ledger, never filtered by a rule written before measurement.

D4: TESTING. When os.environ has CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID, the body carries 'testing': cairn.tools.base.testing_mark.mark(that id), so CC's shim returns it unacted on (Akien: 'testing things are marked as such and we just demand that the system can tolerate and ignore them').

D5: NEVER GATES. Every exception from import, connect or post is caught; one line goes to stderr naming the ticket and the error, and emit returns as before (Law 7: the journal is the record of truth). Proofs live in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ with a stand-in RemoteBus, binding the subject at call time: one tooth for the envelope shape, one for the unreachable bus, one for the testing mark.

D7: A GATE'S PROBES, superseding D6's coined 'handler list'. Akien 2026-10-27: 'each device can add probes to a gate... a list of handlers and data to give them as opposed to probes that are compiled in to pieces of python' and ''handler list' you mean the probes? a probe can be a lot of things. a probe can be a json packet: { event: eventname, message: {event} on {ticket} }, or a surgically implanted piece of code that reports back some metric.' So the gate holds a list of probes, and certification fires each one. This ticket builds the data kind only: a JSON probe {to: <bus address>, event: <eventname>, message: '<template over {event} and {ticket}>'}, fired as one 'personal' envelope to its 'to', whose body is D3's fields plus the rendered message. The code kind (cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe, with trigger/carry callables) is untouched and out of scope here. Today the list holds one probe: {to: 'cc', event: 'certified', message: '{event} on {ticket}'}. Where a gate's probes live is open-413b07bf8322.
